kind: CPU-only source-boundary construction and regression; no live allocation
hypothesis: If a typed observation is already queued when the planner future becomes done, the current while-not-future-done loop can skip the observation monitor and allow an answer based on stale policy assumptions to proceed.
test: Compare the frozen loop condition with a bounded snapshot drain of already-queued events; verify hard invalidation is surfaced, a queued cover terminal is retained, soft events preserve the answer path, and empty backlog returns immediately.
decision: Add a bounded drain at the completed-future boundary and route any invalidation through the existing cancel/discard path.
scope_limits: The baseline race is a deterministic control-flow boundary, not a measured production race frequency.
The focused local test executed the exact added helper extracted from the PR source; the full controller module was not imported in the temporary harness.
A queue snapshot cannot include observations not yet delivered by the reader thread.
No real HUD timing, App Server timing, physical release, task effect, or live threat outcome is established.
counterhypothesis: The completed-future boundary may never coincide with a relevant event backlog in practice, or queued rows may be stale/non-actionable.
allocation: No GPU, model, GUI, live game, or shared desktop resource used.
